what: a bronze sentinel, a copy of Talos, the giant man of bronze that the smith-god Hephaestus made to guard Crete: an ancient Greek bronze statue come to life, cast in metal and nothing else, a tall, broad-shouldered giant with realistic adult proportions, a small head, long limbs, about eight heads tall, two arms and two legs. Every part of him is solid polished bronze metal: his head, face, neck, chest, arms, hands, legs and feet alike, the warm dark gold-brown of an old bronze statue, polished bright on every curve, with dark black-brown patina in the creases and seams. It is metal and not skin anywhere. His head is the cast bronze head of a Greek statue: short tight bronze curls cast in the metal, a straight nose, a stern closed mouth, and two blank staring bronze eyes with no pupils. One raised bronze vein, as thick as a rope, runs down the outside of his right leg from the hip to the ankle, and at the ankle it is stopped by one big round bronze nail head as big as his palm. Both his hands and forearms glow red-hot, bright orange-red like iron fresh from the forge, the dark knuckles showing in the middle of the glow; the rest of him is bronze.
colours: polished warm dark gold-brown bronze over his whole body and head, dark black-brown patina in the creases, blank bronze eyes, red-hot glowing orange-red hands and forearms, one grey granite boulder.
wears: He wears only a short bronze kilt of overlapping metal strips cast as part of him, hanging from a bronze belt to mid-thigh, the same bronze as his body. No helmet, no cloak, no cloth, no shield.
holds: Both his hands together hold exactly one huge rough boulder of grey granite, as big as his own chest, lifted high above his head, his red-hot fingers spread on its underside. Nothing else is in his hands.
pose: On two legs, seen from the side and a little from the front, he strides forward to the left with his weight on his bent front leg and his back leg stretched out behind, his body leaning back as both arms heave the boulder high over his head ready to hurl it forward, his blank bronze face turned toward the viewer.
must_show: a giant man made entirely of polished bronze metal, a Greek statue come alive, head to feet
blank staring bronze statue eyes and cast bronze curls
a grey boulder lifted overhead in both hands, about to be hurled
red-hot glowing hands and forearms
a short bronze kilt, no other clothing

what: a sown warrior, one of the Spartoi, the armed men who sprang up already armed and angry from the dragon's teeth Cadmus sowed: an ancient Greek hoplite, a lean hard grown man with realistic adult proportions, a small head, long limbs, about eight heads tall. His skin is a strange pale ivory white with a faint grey tinge, the dull white of an old tooth, on his face, arms and legs alike, a colour no living man has. His face shows under his open helmet: a furious clean-shaven face with a straight nose, his mouth wide open in a snarl showing clenched white teeth, and two narrow dark eyes full of rage; small round human ears. A few smears of dark mud cling to his bare shins and feet, on his skin only. The face of his shield bears his sign: one huge curved white dragon's fang painted on the bronze, as tall as the shield, pointed at the bottom, plain to see.
colours: pale ivory-white tooth-coloured skin, bright polished bronze helmet and breastplate, a tall black horsehair crest, a short tunic of strong dark red wool, a round bronze shield with one huge white dragon's fang painted on its face, a spear with a dark wooden shaft and a bronze head, a few smears of dark mud on his shins.
wears: He wears the armour of an ancient Greek hoplite: an open-faced bronze helmet with cheek pieces that leaves his face showing, topped with a tall crest of black horsehair running from front to back; a bronze breastplate shaped to the chest; a short tunic of strong dark red wool showing below it as a skirt of flaps to mid-thigh. His legs are bare from the thigh to the feet, pale ivory-white and streaked with earth, and his feet are bare: no shin guards, no boots, no sandals.
holds: On his left forearm he carries exactly one big round bronze shield, as wide as his chest and shoulders, plain polished bronze with a thick rim, held up in front of his body. In his right hand he holds exactly one spear: a long straight dark wooden shaft with a leaf-shaped bronze head, held overhand above his shoulder, flat and horizontal, its point sticking out in front of him at the left; the back end of the spear is a small plain round knob. Nothing else is in his hands.
pose: On two legs, seen from the side and a little from the front, he lunges forward to the left mid-thrust, his weight on his bent front leg and his back leg stretched out behind, the shield held up before him with its painted fang facing the viewer, his right arm driving the spear forward overhand, his snarling face turned toward the viewer; nothing is beneath his feet, the backdrop runs on under him, no ground, no field, no soil.
must_show: a Greek hoplite: crested bronze helmet, bronze breastplate, round bronze shield and spear
his face showing, snarling, pale ivory-white tooth-coloured skin
one big white dragon's fang painted on the shield
a short dark red tunic below the breastplate, bare legs and feet
a lunging spear-thrust
nothing under his feet

what: a madness of Lyssa, the Greek spirit of mad rage and rabies, daughter of Night, whom Hera sent to drive Heracles out of his mind: a wild, terrifying woman-spirit, lean, wiry and fully fleshed, with realistic adult proportions, a small head, long limbs, about eight heads tall, two arms and two legs, plainly not a living woman. Her skin is cold pale ash-grey, the grey of a stone statue, on her face, neck, arms and legs alike. Her face is crazed and frightening: wide-open eyes rolled back so that only the whites show, blank white, a long nose, and a wide open snarling mouth with white teeth, a thick froth of white bubbles foaming over her lips and running down her chin, the mark of rabies. Her hair is a wild tangle of long black hair streaming back from her head, and rearing up out of it round her head are four thick living snakes, each as thick as her wrist and as long as her arm, glossy black with pale yellow bellies, plainly snakes, their heads raised and their mouths open showing white fangs, two on the left of her head and two on the right. Her fingers end in long hooked black claws.
colours: cold pale ash-grey skin, blank white rolled-back eyes, white teeth and white foam at the mouth, wild long black hair with four thick glossy black snakes with pale yellow bellies rearing from it, a short torn chiton of strong dark blood-red cloth, a black cord belt, black claws.
wears: She wears a short chiton of strong dark blood-red cloth that covers her from the shoulders to the knees, belted with a black cord, its hem torn into ragged points that whip about. Her arms and feet are bare. No armour, no crown, no jewels.
holds: Her hands are empty and she holds nothing: both clawed hands are thrust out ahead of her, fingers spread and hooked to rake.
pose: On two legs, seen from the side and a little from the front, she leaps forward through the air to the left in one wild bound, both feet off the ground, her front knee drawn up and her back leg trailing, her body pitched forward, both clawed hands thrust out ahead to rake, her head thrown forward with the foaming mouth wide open, her wild hair and the snakes in it streaming back.
must_show: a wild grey-skinned woman-spirit leaping through the air, clawed hands thrust forward
rolled-back blank white eyes and white foam at the mouth
four thick black snakes rearing from her wild black hair, plainly snakes
a short torn dark blood-red chiton, fully clothed
both hands empty, clawed

what: an ushabti worker, one of the little servant figures of glazed blue faience that were buried in Egyptian tombs to do the dead man's work, risen up man-sized and alive and hard at work: a man of glazed pottery, not a mummy and not a living man, with realistic adult proportions, a small head, about eight heads tall, two arms. Its whole body is one glossy glazed surface of bright turquoise blue-green, like glazed pottery, with small pale chips and crazing cracks in the glaze. Its body is shaped like the lid of a mummy case: from the shoulders down it is one smooth tapering column with no chest, no waist, no hips and no separate legs, narrowing to a small square base; down the front of that column run horizontal bands of black painted hieroglyph signs. Only its two arms are free and they work hard. Its head is glazed the same turquoise: the calm blank face of a man with black painted almond eyes and black painted eyebrows, a straight nose, closed lips, and a short straight black painted beard. On its head is a plain wig painted solid black that falls in two flaps to the chest, with no stripes.
colours: bright glossy turquoise blue-green glaze on the whole body, head and arms, black painted hieroglyph bands, black painted eyes and eyebrows, a plain black painted wig, a hoe with a dark wooden handle and a dull bronze blade, a woven basket of pale straw full of pale sand.
wears: It wears nothing but its glaze: the black wig and the black hieroglyphs are painted on. No collar, no kilt, no headcloth, no bandages.
holds: In its right hand it grips exactly one Egyptian hoe: a short dark wooden handle with one long curved blade of dull brown bronze fixed across its end, curving down like a bird's beak, sticking out to one side only. In its left hand it grips exactly one small round woven basket of pale straw by its rim, flinging it so a spray of pale sand flies out of it toward the viewer. Nothing else is in its hands.
pose: Seen from the side and a little from the front, the column-bodied figure leans far over to the left at a steep slant like a falling post, in the middle of a violent swing: its right arm is raised high above its head with the hoe at the top of the swing about to chop down, and its left arm is flung forward throwing the basket's sand at the viewer, a spray of sand flying from the basket, its calm painted face turned toward the viewer.
must_show: a man-sized glossy turquoise faience figurine, plainly glazed pottery, not a mummy
a column-shaped lower body with black hieroglyph bands down the front, no separate legs
a plain black painted wig, no stripes
one bronze hoe hacked down with both hands
one straw basket of sand hanging from the left forearm
plain: no whip, no headcloth, no kilt
an action pose, bent forward hacking

what: an ushabti overseer, the foreman figurine buried with every ten Egyptian tomb workers to keep them at their labour, grown to the size of a man and come alive: a man-sized figurine of glazed pottery, not a mummy and not a living man, with realistic adult proportions, a small head, long limbs, about eight heads tall, two arms and two legs. Like a real overseer figurine it is made in the dress of the living, not wrapped: it strides on two separate legs. Its whole body is one glossy glazed surface of bright turquoise blue-green, like glazed pottery, with small pale chips and crazing cracks in the glaze, and rows of small black painted hieroglyph signs run in bands round its arms, chest and legs. Its head is a carved figurine's head glazed the same turquoise: a stern face with black painted almond eyes and heavy black painted eyebrows, a straight nose, a hard set mouth, and a short false beard of black glaze on its chin.
colours: bright glossy turquoise blue-green glaze on the whole body, head, arms and legs, black painted hieroglyph bands, black painted eyes and eyebrows, a pharaoh's headcloth striped in broad black and turquoise bands, a stiff triangular kilt of the same glaze with a gold-yellow painted border, a broad painted collar of black and gold-yellow bands, a whip with a black handle and three thick black lashes.
wears: On its head it wears a pharaoh-style striped headcloth that covers the top of the head and falls in two flaps to the chest, striped in broad black and turquoise bands. It wears a stiff triangular kilt that juts forward in a point, glazed turquoise with a gold-yellow painted border, and a broad painted collar of black and gold-yellow bands across its chest. All of it is glaze and paint on the figure. No bandages.
holds: In its right hand, raised high over its head, it holds exactly one overseer's whip: a short thick black handle with three thick black lashes, each as thick as a finger, hanging from its tip and swinging out in a curve. Its left arm is thrust straight out ahead of it, the left hand pointing commandingly with one finger at the viewer, nothing in it. Nothing else is in its hands.
pose: On two legs, seen from the side and a little from the front, it strides forward to the left with its left foot far in front like an Egyptian statue walking, its body upright and stiff, its right arm raised high cracking the whip, its left arm pointing straight out in command, its stern painted face turned toward the viewer.
must_show: a man-sized glossy turquoise faience figurine, plainly glazed pottery, not a mummy
a striped black-and-turquoise headcloth and a short black false beard
a stiff triangular kilt and a painted collar: dressed as the living, striding on two legs
black hieroglyph bands painted on the body
a whip raised in the right hand, the left hand pointing in command
plainly grander than the plain worker

what: a lioness of Sekhmet, one of the Eye of Ra's lionesses that waded in the blood of mankind: a real lioness, an animal on four legs, seen from the side, a huge, powerful, lean hunting lioness with no mane, small round ears, a broad heavy head and a long tail with a dark tuft. Her fur is dusty sand-brown, the dull dun colour of a real lion, paler cream under the chin and belly. Her jaws are wide open in a roar, showing big white fangs; she has just fed, and her muzzle, lips and chin are smeared with bright red blood, with three streaks of it running down her pale throat onto the collar, plain to see against the cream fur. Her eyes are narrow and glow fierce amber. Resting on top of her head, between her ears and touching her head, is one flat solid round disc of polished red copper, as wide as her head, set on edge like a coin, glowing faintly red-orange, the sun disc of Ra; there is no glow or haze around it.
colours: dusty sand-brown fur, the dull dun colour of a real lion, cream under the chin and belly, a dark tail tuft, big white fangs, bright red blood smeared on the muzzle, jaws and throat, glowing amber eyes, a red copper sun disc glowing faintly red-orange on her head, a broad Egyptian collar of gold and dark lapis-blue bands.
wears: Round her neck she wears one broad Egyptian collar, a wide flat half-moon of bands of gold and dark lapis-blue beads lying over her chest and shoulders. Nothing else.
pose: On four legs, seen from the side and a little from the front so all four feet can be seen, she charges forward to the left at full speed, her body stretched long and low to the ground, her back legs gathered under her and her front legs reaching far forward, her head thrust forward at the front of the picture with the bloody jaws wide open in a roar, her front legs reaching forward and her hind legs driving behind; exactly four legs and no more: two front legs and two hind legs, all four shown once each, her tail lashing up behind.
must_show: a real lioness on four legs, side view, no mane
a glowing red-orange sun disc on top of her head
a broad gold and dark blue Egyptian collar
blood on her open roaring jaws
lunging forward

what: a devourer of hearts, one of the brood of Ammit, who crouched beside the scales in the Egyptian Hall of Judgement to eat the hearts of the wicked: a monstrous beast on four legs, seen from the side, made of three animals joined together the way the old Egyptian papyri paint her, each part plainly its own animal and its own colour. Her head is the long head of a crocodile, scaled and armoured, dark olive-green and black, with long jaws full of jagged white teeth and small yellow eyes. Her neck, shoulders, chest and front legs are those of a lion: dusty sand-brown fur, the dull dun colour of a real lion, with a thick dark brown lion's mane round the neck behind the crocodile head, and big lion's paws with claws. Her back half, belly, hind legs and short tail are those of a hippopotamus: smooth, hairless, heavy, rounded hide of dark slate grey, with thick stumpy legs and broad round feet.
colours: a dark olive-green and black scaly crocodile head with white teeth and small yellow eyes, dusty sand-brown lion fur on the shoulders and front legs, a thick dark brown mane, smooth dark slate-grey hippopotamus hide on the back half and hind legs, a small striped Egyptian headcloth of blue and gold behind the crocodile head.
wears: Behind her crocodile head, over the top of the mane, she wears a small Egyptian headcloth striped in blue and gold, as on old paintings of her. Nothing else.
pose: On four legs, seen from the side and a little from the front so all four feet can be seen, she springs forward to the left in a sudden lunge like a crocodile bursting out of the river, her front end dropped low with the lion's front legs splayed wide and bent, her head lowered and thrust far forward at the front of the picture with the long jaws flung wide open to bite, her hindquarters raised behind and driving, the heavy hippopotamus hindquarters behind; exactly four legs and no more: two lion's front legs and two hippopotamus hind legs, all four shown once each.
must_show: a crocodile's head with long open jaws full of teeth
lion's forequarters with a mane and tawny fur
grey hippopotamus hindquarters, plainly a different animal from the front
on four legs, side view, lunging to bite
an Egyptian striped headcloth behind the head

what: one of Takshaka's brood, a naga of Hindu myth in its true form, a serpent of the snake-king Takshaka who hid in a fruit to kill King Parikshit: a great serpent and nothing but a serpent, a real cobra drawn large, long and heavy and immensely strong. Its scales are polished copper, bright metallic copper-brown with an orange sheen on every scale, darker brown between the scales, a paler dull gold belly with broad bands across it. Its head is a cobra's, broad and flat, with a great spread hood behind it, the back of the hood marked with one pale gold spectacle pattern. Its two eyes are round, glossy and pitch-black, with no pupils and no white. Its mouth is open wide, showing two long curved white fangs dripping a little clear venom and a forked red tongue.
colours: polished metallic copper-brown scales with an orange sheen, darker brown between the scales, a pale dull gold banded belly, a pale gold spectacle mark on the hood, glossy pitch-black eyes, long white fangs, a forked red tongue.
pose: The front third of the serpent rears straight up like a cobra, its hood spread wide, its head drawn back and pitched forward toward the left ready to strike, the mouth wide open showing the fangs; the rest of its long thick body lies coiled beneath and behind it in two heavy loops, the tail tip curling out at the right, the whole serpent wholly inside the picture.
must_show: a great copper-coloured cobra and nothing else, hood spread
rearing to strike, mouth open, long white fangs
glossy pitch-black eyes
a heavy coiled body

what: a rakshasa illusionist, one of the demon sorcerers who learned from Indrajit, the son of Ravana, who bound Rama with the serpent noose: a tall, lean, menacing demon man with realistic adult proportions, a small head, long limbs, about eight heads tall, two arms, standing on two legs. He has the whole head of a tiger on a man's body: a tiger's broad face covered in bright orange fur with bold black stripes, only a small patch of white on the chin, never a white tiger and never a man's face, two round tiger's ears on top of his head, a wide pink tiger's nose, long white whiskers, narrow glowing yellow eyes, and a snarling tiger's mouth showing four long white fangs. He has no beard and no human hair. His neck and hands are furred bright orange with black stripes, and his fingers end in long hooked black claws.
colours: bright orange fur with bold black stripes on the head, neck and hands, a small white chin, glowing yellow eyes, white fangs, a long coat of deep crimson silk with heavy gold embroidery, wide trousers of cream silk, a small gold crown, gold necklaces and armlets, a living black snake with pale yellow bands.
wears: He wears the rich court dress of an Indian prince: a long close-fitting coat of deep crimson silk with long sleeves, heavy gold embroidery at the collar, cuffs and hem, covering him from the neck to below the knees; wide trousers of cream silk; several heavy gold necklaces over the coat and gold armlets. On top of his tiger head, between the two round ears, sits a small tall pointed gold crown of a demon prince. No turban. His furred clawed feet are bare.
holds: Between his two hands he holds exactly one living snake, black with pale yellow bands, as thick as his wrist and as long as he is tall, looped into a big noose: its tail is wound round his left fist, its body forms a wide open loop held out in front of him, and its head rears up from his right hand, mouth open, hissing at the viewer. Nothing else is in his hands. He has no staff and no wand.
pose: On two legs, seen from the side and a little from the front, he steps forward to the left with his weight on his front leg, leaning in, both arms thrust out ahead of him casting the snake noose forward like a lasso, his tiger face snarling at the viewer, his coat swinging back.
must_show: a tiger's whole head, bright orange with black stripes, round ears, fangs: plainly a tiger at 64 px
a rich deep crimson and gold Indian coat, fully clothed, with a small gold crown and gold jewellery
one living black-and-yellow snake held between both hands as a noose
clawed striped hands
casting the noose forward

what: a jorogumo, the Japanese spider-demon that lives four hundred years and learns to wear a woman's face: a real spider drawn huge, frightening and uncanny, with the true body of a spider: a small head section in front, a long oval hairy abdomen behind it, longer than it is wide and pointed at its back tip, the abdomen of a real spider and never a ball, and exactly eight long jointed legs, four on each side, black and hairy. The black hair of its abdomen is boldly marked like the silk of a court kimono: broad bands of deep strong red across it with large pale cream flower crests between them. On the front of its head section, where a spider's face would be, is set one flat pale mask-like woman's face, chalk-white like a Noh theatre mask, with thin black painted eyebrows, two narrow black eyes, and a small mouth painted red and open to show black teeth; a fringe of long straight black hair hangs from the head round the mask. Below the mask are two big curved black fangs.
colours: glossy black hairy legs and head section, a long oval abdomen of black hair marked with broad bands of deep strong red and large pale cream flower crests, a chalk-white mask face with black painted eyebrows and eyes and small red lips, long straight black hair round the mask, curved black fangs.
wears: It is a spider and wears nothing; the kimono pattern is the colour of its own abdomen, not cloth.
pose: Seen from the side and a little from the front and above, it rushes forward to the left on its legs, its long abdomen raised high behind it, its body low, its two front legs lifted high and reaching forward over its head to seize, the other six legs spread out under it, the pale mask face turned to stare at the viewer, fangs open.
must_show: a real giant spider with long black hairy legs and a long oval abdomen
the abdomen marked red, black and cream like kimono silk
one chalk-white woman's mask face on the spider's head
front legs raised, reaching to seize
frightening, not pretty

what: a galla, one of the demons of the Sumerian underworld who dragged Inanna's husband Dumuzi down to the land of no return, painted like a creature carved on an old Mesopotamian stone relief brought to life: a lean, wiry, fully fleshed demon with realistic adult proportions, a small head, long limbs, about eight heads tall, two arms, standing on two legs. Its skin is dull grey-brown, the colour of dried river mud, on its face, arms, chest and legs alike, a colour no living person has. Its head is a snarling lion's head on a man's neck: a broad flat lion's face with a short wiry mane of dark brown, wide-open jaws baring big white fangs, a wrinkled snarling muzzle, and two small round staring eyes glowing pale yellow. Its legs end below the knee in the scaly legs of a great bird of prey, dark grey, with three long toes in front, each ending in a long hooked black talon. Its hands end in long hooked black claws.
colours: dull grey-brown skin like dried river mud, a lion's face with a short dark brown wiry mane, pale yellow glowing eyes, white fangs, dark grey scaly bird's legs with black talons, a knee-length kilt of shaggy off-white sheep's fleece hanging in rows of tufts, a broad dark brown leather belt, a club of dark wood.
wears: It wears a Sumerian kilt from the waist to the knee, made of shaggy off-white sheep's fleece hanging in three rows of long tufts one above the other, held up by a broad dark brown leather belt. Its chest, arms and bird's legs are bare. No armour, no helmet, no jewels.
holds: In its right hand, raised high over its head, it holds exactly one club: one straight length of dark wood as long as its arm, narrow at the grip, swelling to a heavy knobbly end, nothing fixed to it. Its left hand is empty: a grey-brown clawed hand thrust far forward at the viewer, fingers spread and hooked to seize. Nothing else is in its hands.
pose: On two legs, seen from the side and a little from the front, it rushes forward to the left with its weight on its bent front leg and its back leg stretched out behind, body pitched forward, its left claw reaching out ahead to grab, its right arm raised high swinging the club, its lion jaws open in a roar at the viewer.
must_show: a lean grey-brown demon with a snarling lion's face
dark scaly bird-of-prey legs with talons
a shaggy fleece Sumerian kilt
one knobbly wooden club raised in the right hand
the left clawed hand empty, grabbing forward

what: a girtablilu, a scorpion-man of Babylonian myth, one of the guardians of the sunrise gate of Mount Mashu that Gilgamesh passed, painted like a figure from an old Babylonian boundary stone brought to life. From the waist up he is a grown man with realistic adult proportions, a small head, long arms: weather-beaten light tan skin, a stern face with a hooked nose and dark eyes, and a long square-cut black beard in tight rows of curls, and long black hair curled at the shoulders. Below his waist, where a man's hips would be, his body becomes the body of a great scorpion lying flat: a long armoured scorpion body of glossy dark brown-black plates stretching out behind him, with jointed scorpion legs along each side, and from its end a thick segmented scorpion tail curves up high over his back, ending in a fat glossy black club with one curved needle-point at its tip. He has no human legs.
colours: weather-beaten light tan skin, a long black square-cut curled beard and black hair, a tall cylindrical cap of dark blue with gold bull's horns round it, a short-sleeved tunic of deep blue wool with a gold fringe, a glossy dark brown-black scorpion body and tail, a bow of dark wood, an arrow with a bronze head.
wears: On his head is a tall flat-topped cylindrical cap of dark blue with three pairs of gold bull's horns curving round it, one pair above the other, the horned crown of a Mesopotamian god. His upper body is covered by a short-sleeved tunic of deep blue wool with a gold fringe, ending at the waist where the scorpion body begins.
holds: He holds exactly one bow: a heavy curved stave of dark wood, as thick as his wrist, one smooth even curve from tip to tip, held upright in his left hand by its middle, out in front of him at the left of the picture, entirely in front of him. In his right hand he holds exactly one arrow with a bronze head, drawn back to his cheek on the bowstring. Nothing else is in his hands.
pose: Seen in full profile like a figure on a coin, facing left, the man's upper body stands upright on the front of the flat scorpion body, drawing the bow at the left, the bow a single D shape entirely in front of him, while the scorpion body stretches out low behind him to the right and the tail arches high over his back with the sting poised to strike forward.
must_show: a bearded man from the waist up on the body of a great scorpion
a horned cylindrical Mesopotamian cap
a blue tunic covering his upper body
a scorpion tail arched over his back with a sting
drawing a bow at the left

what: a stone warrior of Asag, one of the army of stones the Sumerian mountain demon Asag fathered on the mountains, never judged by the god Ninurta: a hunched, neckless thing built entirely of rough grey boulders piled together like a dry-stone wall come alive, with no flesh anywhere and no muscles. Its body is a stack of big jagged grey boulders with slanting broken faces, none of them square and none of them smooth, with dark gaps between them. Each arm is three boulders, one after the other, touching, thicker than its legs, ending in a fist that is one big round boulder with no fingers; each leg is a short pillar of stacked rough slabs, with no feet and no toes. Its head is one lumpy boulder of the very same grey stone, wider than tall, set low between the shoulders, with no face at all: no nose, no mouth, no ears, no brow, no hair; only two small narrow slanted slits glowing orange set in the rock. Every gap and crack between the stones glows faintly orange-red from inside, like embers deep in a fire, so lines of dull orange light run all over the body between the grey stones.
colours: rough dark grey and mid-grey stone with darker shadows, faint orange-red glow in every crack and seam, two small glowing orange eyes.
wears: It wears nothing: it is all stone.
holds: It holds nothing: its fists are its own stones.
pose: On two stone legs, seen from the side and a little from the front, it lunges forward to the left, its weight on its bent front leg, swinging its right boulder fist forward in a huge hook punch toward the viewer, its left boulder fist drawn back low at its side, its faceless head sunk forward between its shoulders.
must_show: a hunched warrior built entirely of rough jagged grey boulders, no flesh
faint orange glow in the cracks between the stones
a faceless boulder head with two small glowing orange slits
fists that are single round boulders, swinging a punch

what: a div of Mazandaran, one of the demons of the Persian Book of Kings who served the White Div and blinded King Kay Kavus with sorcery, painted like a div from an old Persian miniature brought to life: a huge, powerful, heavy-shouldered demon, plainly a monster and never a man, with realistic adult proportions, a small head, long thick arms, two arms, standing on two legs. His skin is dead chalk-white like whitewash, a colour no living man has, and on it, as divs are painted in Persian books, are scattered about twenty big dark brown spots, each as big as his palm and roughly round, on his chest, belly, arms and thighs, wide gaps of white between them. His head is a demon's on a man's skull shape: a broad heavy human-shaped face, never a cat's and never a lion's, with a big hooked nose, a heavy brow, a jutting jaw, two long white tusks curving up from the lower jaw past his cheeks, a wide snarling mouth full of fangs, round staring yellow eyes, long pointed ears, two thick curved horns of black horn rising from his brow, a wild mane of black hair and a short black beard. His fingers end in long hooked black claws.
colours: dead chalk-white skin with about twenty big dark brown spots, black horns, wild black hair and short black beard, white tusks, yellow eyes, a short kilt made of a real leopard's pelt, golden tawny fur covered in black rosettes, with the leopard's tail hanging from it, gold armlets and anklets, a small boiling storm cloud of slate-grey and black with a bright yellow zigzag of lightning.
wears: Round his waist he wears a short kilt made from a real leopard's pelt: golden tawny fur covered in small black rosettes, its ragged edge hanging to the knee and the leopard's long spotted tail hanging down at one side, tied with a gold cord; heavy gold armlets on both upper arms and gold anklets, as divs wear in Persian paintings. No cloth kilt, no brocade. His chest is bare.
holds: His left hand is held out in front of him, palm up, and sitting right in the open palm, touching his fingers, with the fingers curled up into its base, is exactly one small dark storm cloud, slate-grey and black, the size of his head, joined to the hand so that cloud and hand are one shape, with one short bright yellow zigzag of lightning crackling inside it; there is no bowl, no dish and no rock in the hand, only the cloud, and nothing falls from it. His right hand is empty: a white clawed hand raised high, fingers spread and hooked to rake. Nothing else is in his hands. He has no staff, no club and no sword.
pose: On two legs, seen from the side and a little from the front, he stalks forward to the left with his weight on his bent front leg, his left arm thrust forward holding up the storm cloud on his palm toward the viewer, his right clawed hand raised high, his horned head thrust forward with the tusked mouth open in a roar.
must_show: a huge monster with dead chalk-white skin with big dark brown spots
a demon's human-shaped face with tusks, pointed ears, two black horns, wild black hair
a leopard-pelt kilt with rosettes and gold armlets: Persian miniature div
a small storm cloud with lightning sitting in the open left palm, joined to the hand
the right clawed hand empty, raised

what: a khrafstra swarm, the noxious creatures of the Zoroastrian books that poured out of a dragon's wound, piled up together into one heap that crawls forward: exactly five big real animals, each one half as wide as the heap, piled on top of one another and overlapping so that no backdrop shows between them, wholly inside the picture, no one of them bigger than the rest. One thick snake, dull olive-brown with black blotches, loops once through the middle of the heap and rears up at the top with its fanged mouth open. One big glossy black scorpion sits on top at the right with its pincers open and its tail curled high over its back. One fat warty toad, dull grey-brown, squats at the front at the bottom left with its wide mouth open. One dark brown lizard climbs over the left side, head down. One big black wasp with amber stripes and glassy wings clings at the top left. Each animal is drawn whole and plain, big enough to tell what it is.
colours: a dull olive-brown snake with black blotches, a glossy black scorpion, a dull grey-brown warty toad, a dark brown lizard, a black wasp with amber stripes, black gaps between them.
pose: The whole heap crawls forward to the left: the snake rearing to strike, the scorpion with its tail raised and pincers open, the toad lunging with its mouth open, the lizard scrambling over the side, the wasp with its wings up.
must_show: five big recognisable vermin piled together: a snake, a scorpion, a toad, a lizard, a wasp
each animal readable at 64 px
one heap moving forward, no single giant creature

what: a Dahaka wyrm, of the brood of Azhi Dahaka, the three-headed dragon of the Persian Avesta made by the evil spirit to empty the world: a huge, heavy, wingless dragon that walks on all four legs like a huge lizard, its body long, low and horizontal, belly close to the ground, with a long thick tail and no arms. From its broad shoulders rise exactly three long scaled necks, and there are only three heads in the whole picture: the left neck curves up and out to the left, the middle neck goes straight up, the right neck curves up and out to the right, and each ends in one horned dragon head with long open jaws full of fangs; nothing grows lower down on its chest or shoulders. Its scales are dark bronze-brown, the brown of old bronze, darker nearly black along the spine, with a dull pale ochre belly. Its eyes glow fierce yellow. Vermin swarm out of a red gash in its flank and cling all over its body: one big glossy black scorpion as big as one of its heads clinging to its side with its tail raised, one dark brown snake wound twice round its front leg, and one grey-brown toad sitting on its back; each is plain to see against the bronze scales.
colours: dark bronze-brown scales, nearly black along the spine, a dull pale ochre belly, dark horn-grey horns, glowing yellow eyes, white fangs, a dark red wound, black scorpions, a dark brown snake and a grey-brown toad.
pose: Seen from the side and a little from the front so all four feet can be seen, it crawls forward to the left with its body low and horizontal, all four of its feet planted, its three heads lunging out in their three directions with the jaws wide open, its tail sweeping behind it at the right; nothing is under its feet; exactly four legs and no more.
must_show: a dragon with exactly three heads on three long necks
dark bronze-brown scales
on four legs, body low and horizontal, wingless
vermin on it: a black scorpion on its side, a snake round a leg, readable

what: a Totentanz dancer, one of the dancing dead of the medieval Dance of Death that Bernt Notke painted on the church walls of Lubeck and Tallinn after the Black Death, stepped down off the wall: a whole human skeleton with realistic adult proportions, a small skull, long limbs, about eight heads tall, two arms, two legs, bare bones only, no muscle and no flesh. Its bones are old chalk grey-white with dark grey-brown stains, dug from a grave, on the skull, ribs, arms and legs alike, never gold and never yellow. Its skull grins with all its teeth, the eye sockets two black holes. Over one shoulder and round its hips hangs one long torn strip of old grave shroud, dull grey-white linen stained brown, flying out behind it as it dances.
colours: old chalk grey-white bone with dark grey-brown grave stains, black eye sockets, a torn strip of dull grey-white linen shroud stained brown.
wears: It wears only one long torn strip of old linen grave shroud, dull grey-white stained brown, draped over its left shoulder, wound once round its hips and flying out behind it. No armour, no helmet, no crown, no cloak.
holds: Its hands are empty and it holds nothing: its right bony hand reaches out toward the viewer, palm up and fingers open, inviting the viewer to take it and join the dance; its left bony arm is raised high over its skull, the fingers curled as if snapping to the music. It holds no weapon, no scythe, no instrument.
pose: On two legs, seen a little from the front, it dances a lively medieval round-dance step toward the left: its weight on one bent leg, its other leg kicked up high and bent at the knee, its body twisted and swaying, its skull tipped to one side grinning at the viewer, its right hand reaching out to take the viewer's hand, its left arm raised high, the shroud flying.
must_show: a bare skeleton in a lively dance step, one leg kicked up
one bony hand reaching out toward the viewer to take their hand, the other raised high
a torn strip of grave shroud flying from it
both hands empty: no weapon

what: a mara, the nightmare of Norse folk belief that a witch sent to trample King Vanlandi in his sleep, the spirit our word nightmare is named for: a gaunt, long-limbed hag-spirit, painted seriously and frighteningly, plainly not a living woman, with realistic adult proportions, a small head, very long thin arms and legs, two arms and two legs. Her skin is cold blue-grey like a drowned woman, a colour no living person has, stretched thin over her face and long bony hands. Her face is long and gaunt, with hollow cheeks, a long thin nose, ears, a thin-lipped mouth stretched open showing small dark teeth, and two eyes that are the two brightest things in the picture, each a solid spot of pale cold white light with no pupil. Long, thin, tangled grey hair hangs down round her face to the ground. Her long thin fingers end in long dark nails.
colours: cold blue-grey skin like a drowned woman, two pale cold white glowing eyes, long tangled ash-grey hair, a long torn shroud of rags, coal-black in the folds and dark slate-grey on the ridges, with one thin bright line of pale grey light along its edges.
wears: She is wrapped from the neck to the ankles in a long torn shroud of dark rags, coal-black in the folds and dark slate-grey on the ridges, covering her body, arms to the wrists and legs, its ragged ends trailing back behind her. No hood, no armour, no jewels.
holds: Her hands are empty and she holds nothing: both long blue-grey hands are pressed flat downward, fingers spread, bearing her whole weight.
pose: Seen from the side and a little from the front, she crouches low on all fours as if squatting on a sleeper's chest, leaning far forward and down over nothing: her knees bent sharply up under her, both long thin arms straight down in front of her with both hands pressing down hard, her shoulders hunched high and her head pushed forward and low between them, staring up at the viewer with the glowing white eyes, her rags and grey hair hanging down.
must_show: a gaunt blue-grey hag-spirit crouched low, plainly not a living woman
both hands pressing down, bearing her weight
two pale glowing white eyes, the brightest thing in the picture
long tangled grey hair
long dark torn rags covering her, fully clothed
must_not_show: a cloud of mist round her

what: a pale mirror-bright potion in a pilgrim's flask: a flat round glass flask standing on its edge, its body a round disc as wide as it is tall and only a third as thick, seen face-on, with a short narrow neck rising from the top and a small flat oval foot under it, and two small loop handles of dark pewter joining the neck to the shoulders on the left and right. It is filled with a pale silver fluid that seems to reflect the light like a mirror: brightest in the centre, shading to pale grey at the rim, with two broad slanting streaks of white light across it, like sunlight on a window pane, and a faint cool grey tint. The neck has a band of dark pewter and is stopped with a plain dark cork. The glass is thick and the vessel is full nearly to the top, so the whole of it shows the strong colour of what is inside; nothing can be seen through it and the backdrop does not show through it.
colours: Pale mirror-bright silver liquid, brightest at the centre, shading to pale grey at the rim, two broad slanting streaks of white light, dark pewter handles and neck band, a small dark pewter foot, a dark cork.
pose: Standing upright, seen from the front and a little from above.
must_show: flat round pilgrim's flask standing on its edge, with two small loop handles at the neck
pale mirror-bright silver contents with two slanting streaks of light
short neck with a dark cork
